svg.title: Secure views in MotherDuck: control what each user sees.
svg.desc: An analyst runs SELECT * FROM customers on a shared table. A secure view stands in for customers and applies three rules: a WHERE clause keeps only EU rows (row-level security), the SELECT list leaves out email (column-level security), and an expression masks ssn to its last four digits (column masking). The analyst gets three EU rows with masked ssn and no email.

g.text: Consumer queries on customers go through it.
An analyst queries the shared customers table.
The secure view stands in for customers.
A WHERE clause limits which rows consumers see.
A column you leave out of the SELECT doesn't exist for consumers.
An expression in place of a column replaces its values.
The analyst gets only what the view allows.
